q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

Earnings report is August 26, 2026. Today is August 21, 2026. **5 days until resolution.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual reported results) for Q2 FY2027 revenue that will be issued on August 26, 2026.

NVIDIA already issued forward guidance on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, establishing a range of $89.2B–$92.8B.

On August 26, when NVIDIA reports Q1 FY2027 results and provides updated guidance, they will either:
1. **Maintain the $91.0B guidance** (most likely)
2. **Raise guidance** (if Q1 beat was strong and conditions warrant)
3. **Lower guidance** (less likely but possible if demand signals deteriorate)

The research confirms Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6B, which **exceeded guidance**. This is a positive signal but doesn't automatically trigger a raise in Q2 guidance—companies are typically cautious about raising guidance mid-quarter.

The guidance issued in May explicitly assumes **no China Data Center compute revenue**, which is a fixed assumption that's unlikely to change materially in 3 months.

Wall Street consensus is around $91.9B (midpoint of recent estimates), which is only ~1% above NVIDIA's midpoint and well within their already-guided range.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Demand deterioration signals**: Weaker-than-expected data center bookings or inventory concerns post-Q1
- **Macro headwinds**: Economic slowdown, tighter enterprise IT spending
- **Supply chain issues**: Unforeseen manufacturing or logistics problems
- **Competitive pressure**: New AI accelerators from competitors gaining traction
- **Conservative bias**: NVIDIA might lower to provide easier beat target

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Q1 beat momentum**: Strong sequential revenue growth ($81.6B vs. prior quarters) may justify raising the bar
- **Data center strength**: If customer demand signals and pipeline data remain robust
- **China tariff/export clarification**: If geopolitical restrictions ease, removing the embedded "no China" assumption
- **Market share gains**: If NVIDIA is taking GPU market share faster than previously expected
- **Confidence from close visibility**: With August already well underway, NVIDIA has high visibility into Q2 results

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides one directly relevant data point:
- **May 20, 2026 guidance**: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B–$92.8B floor/ceiling)
- **Q1 FY2027 actual**: $81.6B (exceeded guidance, magnitude of beat not specified but implied to be positive)

No other historical base rates are provided in the research for how often NVIDIA raises/maintains/lowers guidance between reporting quarters. Standard practice in tech is to maintain or slightly raise guidance post-beat unless conditions deteriorate, but NVIDIA is known for conservative guidance.

---

## Reasoning on the range

The question's range is **99.5B–115.5B**, which extends well above the $92.8B ceiling of NVIDIA's existing guidance. This suggests the questioner is asking about the possibility of a significant guidance raise.

However, given that:
1. The May guidance was just issued 3 months ago
2. Q1 beat, while positive, was not catastrophic (revenue ~$81.6B)
3. Only 5 days have passed since my knowledge cutoff relative to the earnings date
4. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) is only 1% above the midpoint
5. Companies rarely raise guidance dramatically in mid-quarter updates

The **most probable outcome is that NVIDIA maintains or slightly raises guidance in the $90B–$94B range**, centering near **$91B–$92.5B**.

The upper tail of the question's range (above $100B) would require either:
- A massive Q1 beat with strong forward signals
- A major China export restriction removal (lifting the "no China" assumption)
- Unprecedented acceleration in data center demand

These are possible but not the base case. I estimate roughly:
- 65–70% probability guidance stays in $89.2B–$94B range (current or modest raise)
- 20–25% probability guidance raises to $94B–$100B (strong beat signals)
- 10% probability guidance outside these bounds (either major cut or major raise)

Given the question range starts at 99.5B, the median should be anchored to the most likely scenario (~$91.5B midpoint) with upside tail probability for larger raises.

---

## Final Estimate

**Low (10th percentile):** 88500000000
**Median (50th percentile):** 91500000000
**High (90th percentile):** 96500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to report its fiscal Q2 FY2027 results on August 26, 2026, after market close [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own forward guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This range implies a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), with some aggregators pegging it closer to $93.5 billion [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). This average is within NVIDIA's guided range, about 1% above the midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).
